messages:
noah: quick PSA 11 my fern decided to expand into my ethernet cable and now my router is in witness protection. posting for sympathy and tips. pic: https://imgur.com/fernfall123

talia: oh noooo 622343 which fern species is this, for science? also try reseating the cable at both ends.

marco: been there. if you see link flapping after a plant event, try a factory reboot on the router UI, then power-cycle modem. sometimes DHCP gets weird.

noah: tried reseat and soft reboot. still getting `no route to host` intermittently. ISP says nothing reported in my area. very suspicious plant.

jen: interim: tether to phone and use a hotspot. bonus: you can stream a plant documentary while you fix it. :smile:

infra-bot: Tip: if networking affects customer-facing services, run `redwood status report --impact=high` and tag @oncall.

talia: another idea: try swapping the cable. I had a cheap CAT5e go flaky after a cat used it as a chew toy.

noah: swapped to spare cable, status improved but occasional packet loss. ordered a new cable + a short USB-C ethernet dongle just in case.

marco: pro move: Velcro the router to a higher shelf. plants climb, routers don't.

jen: mini-poll: who else has a green coworker that attacks hardware? react with :herb: if yes.

noah: :herb: thanks for the suggestions y'all. will report back with fern containment status. also accepted offers of spare cables DM'd.

talia: please set up a tiny warning sign for the fern: "Do not excavate the ethernet".

noah: adding to calendar: Fern Containment 2pm Thursday (optional).

infra-bot: If this escalates to an outage, the incident channel is #incidents. For non-urgent hardware help, tag #eng-infra.
